task: Build the Assistant's MCP server: an MCP server the user's own Assistant connects to, exposing edit, validate, test-connection, run, Preview and read-logs tools for dev and Branch Environments only. Stage and prod requests are refused in the server's own code (ADR-0009), and tests assert that no MCP response contains a secret value. Settle first what the Assistant needs beyond those six tools, and how server code reliably tells a dev/Branch request from a stage/prod one.

analysis.objective: Ship an `adops mcp` stdio MCP server, registered by an init-written .mcp.json, whose run, preview and validate tools act only on the Environment named exactly `dev` or a Branch Environment, refuse every other Environment and any dev that shares a database with stage or prod in server code, fail fast on a held Warehouse lock, and never return a secret value — the first slice of vision item 7; the remaining Assistant tools follow in the next horizon.
analysis.successDefinition: This horizon is done when ALL hold: (1) `adops mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio, and `adops init` / `adops init --demo` write a .mcp.json registering it (pinned by init tests and the ci.yml wheel list). (2) The server lists exactly the tools run, preview and validate. run and preview accept only the Environment named exactly `dev` or a branch name; unit tests show stage, prod, qa, production, Dev, 'dev ' and a custom name each get a sanitized refusal before any Warehouse, Source, target or file is touched. (3) run and preview on dev are refused when dev's Warehouse or any dev Reverse Sync target is the same database connection as stage's or prod's (normalized Postgres host/port/database, resolved DuckDB path), with a test per case; the demo Project's dev uses its own shop_dev target so the demo is not refused. (4) A Branch run through MCP works when stage's Warehouse Secret Reference is set, fails with a sanitized error naming it when not, only ever Previews, and returns 'stage is busy' at once when stage's Warehouse lock is held (the CLI keeps its 30-minute wait). (5) An in-memory MCP secret-leak suite sets a distinctive value for every Secret Reference and asserts no response of run, preview or validate, on success and failure paths (invalid YAML, missing Secret Reference, unreachable Warehouse, unexpected error), contains any secret value. (6) Engine output never reaches the stdio protocol stream. (7) CI stays green: uv sync --locked with mcp in pyproject.toml and uv.lock, ruff, 100% line+branch coverage, no new pragma, no mcp/typer imports in domain/application, Docker E2E within 20 minutes. The remaining vision item-7 tools (edit, read/list files, project view, test-connection, read-logs, drop-branch, accept-schema) and run logs are later horizons.
assumptions: confirmed: Environment rule is an allow-list. MCP tools accept only the Environment named exactly `dev` (case-sensitive, no trimming) or a Branch Environment selected by a branch name. Every other name is refused in server code.
confirmed: the server also refuses dev when dev's Warehouse or any of dev's Reverse Sync targets is the same database connection as stage's or prod's.

confirmed: the extra tools are a read-only Project view (Pipelines, Steps, Environments, each Secret Reference name and whether it is set), read/list Project files, drop a Branch Environment (br_<branch>__ schemas only), and accept-schema for dev only.
confirmed: edit/read/list may touch only pipelines/, dbt/ and adops.yaml. They refuse .env, .adops/, .github/, server/ and anything outside the Project, including symlink and `..` escapes.
confirmed: every run (CLI and MCP) writes a cleaned, secret-free log to .adops/logs/<env>/<run>.log. read-logs lists and reads only those files. Dagster internals are not exposed.
confirmed: a Branch run from a laptop is allowed when stage's Warehouse password Secret Reference is set locally. Otherwise it fails with a sanitized error naming that Secret Reference.
confirmed: a new `adops mcp` command runs the server over stdio, and `adops init` writes a .mcp.json that registers it for Claude Code.
confirmed: the user chose the MCP server for horizon 9 over the horizon-8 brief's recommendation to harden Promotion and build ADR-0015 records first. Those blockers stay open.
The Environment and path rules are pure domain policy (no framework imports), so they can be tested at 100% branch coverage. The MCP SDK appears only in interface/infrastructure, per guard g6.

The MCP tools call the same code paths the CLI already uses (run_in_environment/_run_branch, validate, accept_schema, drop_branch) rather than shelling out to the adops CLI, so a refusal sits in front of the same code path and existing sanitized errors (RUN_ERRORS) are reused.

test-connection does not exist yet. It becomes a new use case that opens and closes each Source, the Warehouse and each Reverse Sync target of the requested dev/Branch Environment, behind ports, and returns reachable/unreachable plus the existing fixed sanitized messages.

The preview tool runs the requested Pipeline in dev or the Branch Environment and returns the existing Reverse Sync Preview (at most 5 keys per kind plus changed column names, never values). In those Environments it never writes, because only stage and prod write (horizon-5 decision).

A Branch Environment reached through MCP is built exactly as `adops run --branch` builds it: stage's Warehouse, br_<branch>__ schemas, deferring unchanged Steps to stage, taking stage's Warehouse lock.

A secret value is any value currently resolved for a Secret Reference used by the Project's adops.yaml. The leak test injects distinctive values and scans the full serialized MCP response (content, structured content, error text).
An edit is a whole-file write (or create) within the allowed paths. After an edit the Assistant calls validate itself; edit does not run validation automatically.
The Environment and shared-connection rules are checked on every Environment-touching tool call against adops.yaml as it is at call time, so an edit to adops.yaml cannot leave a bypass in place.
MCP behaviour is tested with the SDK's in-memory client/server transport in the unit suite. At most a short stdio smoke test is added, so the Docker E2E budget is not consumed.
The .adops/logs/ files are git-ignored, like the rest of .adops/.
confirmed: the demo Project's dev Environment gets its own Reverse Sync target database shop_dev, so the strict shared-connection rule refuses nothing in the demo.
The plain template gains a .gitignore (.env, .adops/) so run logs are ignored in plain Projects too.
risks: A Branch Environment lives in stage's Warehouse and needs stage's Warehouse password locally, so only server code keeps writes inside br_<branch>__ schemas. A bug in schema routing or drop-branch's prefix match could damage stage's own schemas; needs explicit tests that stage schemas are untouched.
A Branch Environment uses stage's Reverse Sync targets, so a Branch Preview reads stage's operational target databases. The Preview-only guarantee must be re-asserted at the MCP layer.

Detecting 'the same database connection' is best effort: DNS aliases, IP vs name, Docker host aliases can point at one server undetected. Normalization covers localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 and resolved DuckDB paths only.

Symlink and path-escape checks are easy to get subtly wrong: symlinked parents, case-insensitive macOS filesystems (`.ENV`, `Pipelines/`), Unicode normalization. Paths must be resolved and compared after resolution.

Secret leaks can come through channels the CLI never exercised: MCP error payloads built from exception messages, dbt/dlt text in the new log files, read-file contents (a literal password typed into an allowed file would be returned), and the Project view.
Runs are long, and a Branch run can wait up to 30 minutes for stage's Warehouse lock, which can exceed the Assistant's MCP tool-call timeout and leave a half-finished run with no visible result.
Dagster, dlt and dbt write to stdout; over a stdio MCP transport any stray stdout write corrupts the JSON-RPC stream. Engine output must be redirected away from stdout while the server runs.
Adding the MCP Python SDK may pull dependency versions (anyio, pydantic, starlette, httpx) that conflict with the existing dagster/dlt/dbt-core lock; guard g1 then fails.
Reaching 100% line and branch coverage over an async SDK-driven server and the new logging path takes noticeable test effort; g6 forbids pragmas, so stdio entry-point glue must still be covered.
Writing a log file for every CLI run changes existing run behaviour; existing tests and the Docker E2E may need updates.
Users whose dev Environment is named differently (e.g. `development`) get every MCP tool refused; the refusal message must explain it.
accept-schema for dev only leaves the accept-schema --branch gap and ADR-0015 unknowns open.

The optional Analytics Agent and any LLM key: ADR-0002 keeps the core LLM-free.
The Verified Source E2E suite and the single-VM production playbook: later vision items.

phases.name: Add the Assistant Environment rules
phases.goal: One pure domain module decides, with no I/O, whether an MCP tool call from the Assistant may act on an Environment: only exactly `dev`, or a Branch Environment chosen by a branch name, and never when dev shares a database connection with stage or prod.
phases.rationale: Every MCP tool must refuse stage, prod and custom Environments in server code, before anything is touched. Keeping the rules pure and framework-free lets the unit suite test every refusal case at 100% branch coverage, and puts all later tools behind one shared definition of 'allowed'. The file-path rule is not built here; it ships with the file tools that use it.
changes: Create src/adops/domain/assistant_access.py with an `AssistantRefusal` exception that carries only a fixed, sanitized message (an Environment name or a path the caller supplied, never a connection value or secret).

Add `assistant_target(environment: str | None, branch: str | None) -> AssistantTarget`. An `AssistantTarget` is a small frozen dataclass saying 'dev' or 'branch <name>'. It accepts `environment == "dev"` exactly (case-sensitive, no trimming) or a non-empty branch with no environment. It raises `AssistantRefusal` for every other case: `stage`, `prod`, `qa`, `production`, `Dev`, `dev `, any custom name, both given, or neither given. Treat 'neither given' as dev only if the tool layer passes 'dev' explicitly, so the rule itself stays explicit. The refusal message says the Assistant works only in the Environment named exactly `dev` or in a Branch Environment, so a user whose dev Environment is called `development` understands why.

Add `refuse_shared_dev_connection(environments, duckdb_identity)`. Using the `ProjectSettings.environments` mapping from domain/environment.py, it raises `AssistantRefusal` when dev's Warehouse, or any of dev's Reverse Sync targets, is the same database connection as stage's or prod's Warehouse or any of their targets. 'Same connection' for Postgres means the same host, port and database after the host is lowercased and localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 are treated as one host. For DuckDB it means equal strings returned by the `duckdb_identity` callable that the caller injects. The caller resolves each path to an absolute path, because domain code may not touch the filesystem.

Write tests/unit/domain/test_assistant_access.py with one test per refusal and acceptance case of assistant_target (dev, branch, stage, prod, qa, production, Dev, 'dev ', custom, both given, neither given), plus shared-connection cases: the same Warehouse, the same target, a target equal to stage's Warehouse, a localhost-versus-127.0.0.1 alias, an equal DuckDB identity, a prod that is not configured, and fully separate connections that pass.
phases.expectedResult: src/adops/domain/assistant_access.py with branch-complete unit tests proving every allowed and refused Environment and shared-connection case.
guardNotes: g6: the module imports only from adops.domain and the standard library modules the purity test allows (no os, pathlib, mcp or typer). DuckDB path resolution is injected as a callable.
g3: every branch of the three rules has a test; no pragma.

rubric.label: Only exact dev or a Branch Environment is accepted
rubric.ruleStatement: Derived from the acceptance criterion 'The MCP server's tools act only for dev and Branch Environments': assistant_target(environment, branch) returns an AssistantTarget only for environment == "dev" exactly (with no branch) or for a non-empty branch with no environment, and raises AssistantRefusal for everything else. 10 = every case in the matrix below is a separate named test, and the refusal text explains the exact-`dev` rule. 8 = all cases are refused correctly and tested, with some grouped into one parametrized test. Below 8 = any non-dev name is accepted.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/unit/domain/test_assistant_access.py -q` passes.

In a Python shell, `from adops.domain.assistant_access import assistant_target, AssistantRefusal`: assistant_target('dev', None) and assistant_target(None, 'feature-x') both return an AssistantTarget; the second one records the branch name 'feature-x'.

Each of assistant_target('stage', None), ('prod', None), ('qa', None), ('production', None), ('Dev', None), ('dev ', None), ('development', None), ('dev', 'x'), (None, None) and (None, '') raises AssistantRefusal.
The message of str(AssistantRefusal) for ('development', None) contains the literal `dev` and says that only the Environment named exactly `dev` or a Branch Environment is allowed.
AssistantTarget is a frozen dataclass: setting an attribute on an instance raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError.
failureExamples: The value is .strip()ed or .lower()ed before comparing, so 'Dev' or 'dev ' is accepted. This is a plausible honest attempt to be 'helpful'.
When neither argument is given, the code quietly defaults to dev instead of refusing.
An empty-string branch is accepted as a Branch Environment.
Both environment and branch are given and the branch silently wins.

rubric.label: Shared dev database detection is correct and complete
rubric.ruleStatement: refuse_shared_dev_connection raises AssistantRefusal whenever dev's Warehouse or any dev Reverse Sync target is the same connection as stage's or prod's Warehouse or any of their targets. For Postgres, 'same' means host (lowercased, with localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 treated as one host), port and database. For DuckDB, it means equal results from the injected identity callable. 10 = all of these pairings are tested, including cross pairings (dev target vs stage Warehouse) and a missing prod. 8 = the pairings are correct and tested, but one alias or cross pairing is untested. Below 8 = a shared database gets through.
passCriteria: Tests exist and pass for: the same Warehouse; the same target; a dev target equal to stage's Warehouse; 'LOCALHOST' vs '127.0.0.1' vs '::1' on the same port and database; an equal DuckDB identity; prod not configured (no error); fully separate connections (no error).
A test with the same host and database but a different port, and one with the same host and port but a different database, both pass with no refusal (no false positive).
The DuckDB comparison calls the injected `duckdb_identity` callable. A test passes a fake callable that maps two different relative strings to one identity and expects a refusal.

phases.name: Add the adops mcp server with a run tool
phases.goal: A new `adops mcp` command starts an MCP server over stdio that the Assistant can connect to. Its first tool, `run`, runs a Pipeline in dev or a Branch Environment, after the Environment and shared-connection rules have been checked against adops.yaml as it is at call time. A test harness proves that no MCP response contains a secret value.
phases.rationale: This is the smallest server the Assistant can actually use, and it fixes the safety pattern every later tool copies: refuse first, never pass raw exception text through, keep engine output off the JSON-RPC stream. `run` reuses the run code path the CLI already uses, so refusals sit in front of real behaviour from day one. It also adds a backward-compatible lock_timeout keyword to the existing run code path so the Assistant gets an immediate 'busy' reply instead of a 30-minute wait; the CLI keeps waiting.
changes: Add `mcp>=1.30,<2` to the runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml and regenerate uv.lock with `uv lock` in the same change.

Create src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py. It builds a `FastMCP` server for a Project folder and has an `mcp(project: Path = Path("."))` typer command that serves it over stdio. Register the command in cli.py with `app.command()(mcp)`.

Write every tool as a plain synchronous function. FastMCP then runs tool calls one at a time on its event loop. This matters because run_project swaps os.environ in place, which is not safe if two calls run at once.

Protect the stdio JSON-RPC stream (the channel MCP messages travel on). At server start, duplicate file descriptor 1 for the protocol and point file descriptor 1 at stderr for the server's lifetime. Anything Dagster, dbt or dlt prints to stdout then goes to stderr. Unit-test this helper: a write to `sys.stdout` and a raw `os.write(1, ...)` inside it must both land on stderr.

Add one guard helper that every Environment-touching tool calls first. It re-reads adops.yaml, calls `assistant_target`, and for dev calls `refuse_shared_dev_connection` with a DuckDB identity that resolves `project / path` to an absolute path. Only after both pass does it hand back the arguments for `run_project`: environment `dev`, or branch `<name>` (which builds the Branch Environment from stage exactly as `adops run --branch` does).

Add an optional `lock_timeout` keyword to `run_project` (default: the existing 30-minute DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT from warehouse_lock.py) and pass it through `_holding_lock` to `build_warehouse_lock`/`warehouse_lock(timeout=...)`. The CLI keeps the default. The MCP `run` tool passes 0, so when the Warehouse lock (stage's, for a Branch run) is already held, the tool returns at once with the existing WarehouseLocked message turned into a plain 'stage is busy, try again later' reply instead of hanging. Test the CLI default is unchanged and the MCP busy reply.

Add the `run` tool (pipeline, environment, branch). It calls `run_project` from run_command.py, never `run()` or `_run_one`. It returns a plain dict built from RunResult/StepReport/ReverseSyncPreview fields: step name, status, checks, rows loaded, the already-redacted error, and preview counts with sample keys. If any step reports `preview.written is True`, it returns a refusal error instead, which keeps Preview-only true at this layer.

Catch every exception inside each tool and return a sanitized MCP error. Use `error_lines(error)` for RUN_ERRORS and `AssistantRefusal`, and only `unexpected <TypeName>` for anything else. Never let FastMCP turn `str(exception)` into a response.

Create tests/unit/interface/mcp_harness.py. It writes a Project whose .env sets a distinctive value for every Secret Reference (every password_env in every Environment plus alert_webhook_env). It opens an in-memory session with `mcp.shared.memory.create_connected_server_and_client_session`, and it provides `assert_no_secret(result)`, which scans the full serialized response (content, structured content, error text). Tests use `@pytest.mark.anyio` with an `anyio_backend` fixture returning 'asyncio'.

In test_mcp_server.py, reuse the `run_command.build_*` monkeypatch seams and the FakeLocks `locks` fixture. Cover: run in dev; run in a branch; a refusal for each disallowed Environment before any build_* seam is called; a shared-connection refusal; a missing stage Warehouse Secret Reference for a branch run, giving a sanitized error that names it; an invalid YAML error; an unreachable Warehouse; and an unexpected exception reduced to its type name. Pass every response through `assert_no_secret`. Cover the stdio entry point with a CliRunner test that monkeypatches the server's run call, with no pragma.
inputs: mcp 1.30.0 (FastMCP, in-memory session), already verified against uv.lock
phases.expectedResult: A working `adops mcp` stdio server exposing a `run` tool that refuses every Environment except exact `dev` and Branch Environments, with in-memory MCP tests that assert no response contains a secret value.
guardNotes: g1: pyproject.toml and uv.lock change together via `uv lock`, so `uv sync --locked` passes.
g2: follows ruff E,F,W,I,B,UP at line length 100.
g3: the stdio entry point, the stdout redirect and every error-mapping branch are covered by unit tests; no pragma.
g6: mcp is imported only in src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py; domain and application gain no imports.

rubric.label: Stage, prod and custom are refused in code before anything is touched
rubric.ruleStatement: Verbatim acceptance criterion: 'Stage and prod requests are refused in the server's own code (ADR-0009), not by prompt instructions.' The `run` tool's guard re-reads adops.yaml at call time, calls assistant_target, and for dev calls refuse_shared_dev_connection, all before any build_* seam, lock or run_project call. 10 = every disallowed name and the shared-connection case have a test asserting that zero seams were called and no lock was taken, plus a test that an adops.yaml edited between two calls changes the outcome. 8 = refusals are tested with seam spies, but the call-time re-read is untested. Below 8 = any refusal depends on a tool description or docstring, or happens after a seam runs.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py -q` passes.

Tests call `run` with environment 'stage', 'prod' and a custom name (for example 'qa'), and with a dev that shares a database with stage. Each asserts the response is an error AND that the monkeypatched run_command.build_* spies and the FakeLocks fixture recorded no calls.
A test changes adops.yaml after the server starts (for example, it makes dev share stage's target) and the next `run` call is refused. This proves the guard does not use settings cached at startup.
`grep -n 'stage\|prod' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows no refusal that depends only on a tool description string. The decision comes from adops.domain.assistant_access.
failureExamples: adops.yaml is loaded once in the server factory, so a later edit that makes dev share stage's database is not caught. This is a plausible optimisation.
The refusal is raised inside run_project after build_orchestrator() has already run.
The `environment` parameter is typed as Literal['dev'], so the only 'refusal' is FastMCP's schema validation error, and the server has no refusal code of its own.

rubric.label: Tests prove no MCP response carries a secret value
rubric.ruleStatement: Verbatim acceptance criterion: 'Tests assert that no MCP response contains a secret value.' mcp_harness.py seeds a distinctive .env value for every Secret Reference in the Project, and assert_no_secret scans the whole serialized CallToolResult (content, structuredContent, isError text). Every `run` test passes its result through it, and unexpected exceptions are reduced to 'unexpected <TypeName>'. 10 = the harness is itself tested with a negative case that plants a secret in a fake result and expects assert_no_secret to fail. 8 = every test uses the harness, but it has no self-test. Below 8 = any test response is not scanned, or an unexpected-exception message passes str(error) through.
passCriteria: tests/unit/interface/mcp_harness.py writes a .env that sets a unique value for every password_env of every Environment AND for alert_webhook_env.

Every test in test_mcp_server.py that calls a tool calls assert_no_secret on the result. Check with `grep -c assert_no_secret tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py`, which should be at least the number of call_tool uses.
A test makes a build_* seam raise RuntimeError('<seeded secret value>'). The response text is exactly or contains 'unexpected RuntimeError' and passes assert_no_secret.
A test with a missing stage Secret Reference for a branch run returns an error that names the Secret Reference (the env var name) and not any value.
failureExamples: assert_no_secret checks only result.content[0].text and misses structuredContent. This is a plausible partial scan.
Only the Warehouse password is seeded, so a leak of the alert webhook value or a Reverse Sync target password would go unnoticed.
A generic `except Exception as e: return {'error': str(e)}` is used, which leaks connection strings that contain passwords.

rubric.label: A held Warehouse lock returns at once from MCP, and the CLI keeps waiting
rubric.ruleStatement: run_project takes lock_timeout (default DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT) and passes it down to warehouse_lock. The MCP `run` tool passes 0 and turns WarehouseLocked into a plain 'stage is busy, try again later' style reply. `adops run` keeps the 30-minute default. 10 = both behaviours are tested, including a Branch run where stage's lock is held, and the busy reply passes assert_no_secret. 8 = both are tested for dev or branch only. Below 8 = the MCP tool can block on a held lock.
passCriteria: A test holds the lock through the FakeLocks fixture and calls the MCP `run` tool. The call returns an error whose text says the Environment (stage, for a branch) is busy and to try again later, and no orchestrator seam ran.
A test asserts that the CLI path (`adops run` through CliRunner, or run_project called without lock_timeout) passes timeout == DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT to the lock builder.
`grep -n 'lock_timeout' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows lock_timeout=0 passed on every run_project call.
failureExamples: lock_timeout is added to run_project but not passed through _holding_lock, so the MCP call still waits 30 minutes. This is a plausible plumbing miss.
The default is changed globally to 0, which breaks the CLI's waiting behaviour.
The raw WarehouseLocked message, which contains the lock file path or connection details, is returned as is.

rubric.label: Engine output cannot corrupt the stdio protocol
rubric.ruleStatement: At server start, file descriptor 1 is duplicated for the MCP protocol and fd 1 is pointed at stderr for the server's lifetime, so prints from Dagster, dbt or dlt (from Python or from a subprocess) never reach the JSON-RPC stream. 10 = a unit test proves both a sys.stdout write and a raw os.write(1, ...) land on stderr while the protocol writer still reaches the original stdout. 8 = the redirect is tested for both write paths, but not for the protocol side. Below 8 = only sys.stdout is redirected (for example with contextlib.redirect_stdout).
passCriteria: A test enters the stdout-protection helper, runs `print('x')` and `os.write(1, b'y')`, and captures both on stderr (capfd), with neither on stdout.
Running `grep -n 'os.dup\|dup2' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows an fd-level redirect, not just contextlib.redirect_stdout.
A CliRunner test invokes `adops mcp` with the server's stdio run call monkeypatched, and the command exits 0, which proves it is registered in cli.py.
failureExamples: contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) is used. It passes a print test but lets dbt's subprocess output corrupt the stream. This is a plausible miss.
fd 1 is redirected but the protocol is not given the saved duplicate, so the server writes its JSON-RPC to stderr and the client hangs.

rubric.label: The run tool reports only redacted fields and keeps Preview-only
rubric.ruleStatement: The `run` tool returns a plain dict built from RunResult, StepReport and ReverseSyncPreview fields (step name, status, checks, rows loaded, the redacted error, preview counts and sample keys). It turns RUN_ERRORS and AssistantRefusal into error_lines output, and returns a refusal if any step reports preview.written is True. 10 = each mapping branch has a test, including written=True. 8 = written=True is tested and the error mapping is correct, but one RUN_ERRORS class is untested. Below 8 = a dev or branch run that reported a write returns success.
passCriteria: A test makes the fake reverse-sync seam return a ReverseSyncPreview with written=True. The tool response is an error and reports no step success.
Tests cover an invalid adops.yaml and an unreachable Warehouse. Each returns the same lines error_lines() gives for that exception.
The success response for a dev run is JSON-serialisable (json.dumps works) and has no dataclass or exception objects in it.
failureExamples: The tool returns dataclasses.asdict(result), which carries every field, including any future raw value field. This is a plausible shortcut.
written=True is logged but still returned as success.

rubric.label: The MCP SDK and run orchestration sit only in the interface layer
rubric.ruleStatement: `mcp` is imported only in src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py and in tests. The tool calls run_command.run_project, not the CLI `run()` command or `_run_one`. Domain and application gain no imports. Tools are synchronous functions, so calls run one at a time. 10 = all of these hold, and the dependency is declared in pyproject.toml within mcp>=1.30,<2. 8 = all hold except one tool written as `async def` that only awaits sync code. Below 8 = mcp is imported outside interface, or a tool calls the typer command.
passCriteria: `grep -rnE '^(from|import) mcp' src/adops` lists only src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py.
`grep -nE 'async def' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows no tool function defined with async def.
`grep -nE '\brun\(|_run_one' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows no call to the CLI run command or _run_one. run_project is used instead.
`git diff --stat` shows no change under src/adops/domain or src/adops/application in this phase. The `uv sync --locked` gate passes.
failureExamples: A shared 'mcp_errors.py' helper is put in adops/application and imports mcp.types. This is a plausible refactor that breaks the layering.
The tool invokes the typer `run` command and parses its echoed output.

phases.healerHint: If secret or refusal tests fail, move the guard into one `_guarded_args(project, environment, branch)` helper called as the first line of the tool, and wrap the whole tool body in a single try/except that maps AssistantRefusal and RUN_ERRORS through error_lines and everything else to f'unexpected {type(e).__name__}'.

The pinned plain and demo file sets include it. 10 = a fresh init in each mode, run from the installed wheel, produces the file. 8 = this is proven through the unit tests and the source tree only. Below 8 = one mode lacks the file, or it lands under a different name.
passCriteria: `uv run adops init <tmp1>` and `uv run adops init --demo <tmp2>` both create <tmp>/.mcp.json.
`grep -n '.mcp.json' tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py` shows it in DEMO_FILES and in the plain file set.
`grep -n '.mcp.json' .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows it in the demo loop and as plain/.mcp.json in the plain loop. Guard outcome: the wheel listing has both.
failureExamples: The file is added only to templates/demo, which forgets plain Projects. This is a plausible miss because the demo is the usual test path.
The wheel build drops dotfiles. The source-tree unit test passes, but `pip install` users get no .mcp.json.

rubric.label: The registration lives in template files, not in init code
rubric.ruleStatement: The .mcp.json content lives only as template files. init_command.py is unchanged, unless a RENAMED entry (for example 'mcp.json' to '.mcp.json') is needed because the wheel drops dotfiles. No JSON is built in Python, and init's empty-folder refusal still applies. 10 = init_command.py is untouched, or changed only by that RENAMED entry backed by a wheel check. 8 = a RENAMED entry was added as a precaution without checking. Below 8 = init code writes the JSON itself.
passCriteria: `git diff src/adops/interface/init_command.py` is empty, or changes only the RENAMED mapping.
`grep -rn 'mcpServers' src/adops --include=*.py` returns nothing.
The existing test that init refuses a non-empty folder still passes, and no .mcp.json is written in that case.
failureExamples: A `_write_mcp_json(target)` helper is added to init_command.py that calls json.dump. It works, but it duplicates template data in code and is skipped by the wheel template checks. This is a plausible design slip.

phases.healerHint: If .mcp.json is missing from the wheel or the init output, follow the existing `gitignore` to `.gitignore` pattern: ship it as `mcp.json` and add a RENAMED entry, then update both ci.yml loops to the shipped name.

phases.name: Add the preview and validate MCP tools
phases.goal: The server gains `validate`, which checks a Pipeline or the whole Project without connecting to anything, and `preview`, which runs a Pipeline in dev or a Branch Environment and returns only the Reverse Sync Preview: counts, at most 5 sample keys per kind, and changed column names, never row values.
phases.rationale: After an edit, the Assistant's normal loop is validate, then look at what a Reverse Sync would change. Both tools reuse existing code (validate_project and run_project), so they are thin additions on top of the guard and serializer built with `run`.
changes: Add a synchronous `validate(pipeline: str | None)` tool. It calls `validate_project(project, pipeline)` from validate_command.py and returns the Report's problems, skipped Pipelines and Schedules as plain lists. It takes no Environment, because validation never connects.

Add a synchronous `preview(pipeline, environment, branch)` tool. It goes through the same guard helper as `run`, calls `run_project`, and returns only each Reverse Sync step's Preview fields, plus any failing step's redacted error. It refuses if any Preview reports `written`.
In preview's serializer copy only PreviewSample's keys (capped at PREVIEW_SAMPLE_SIZE per kind, as defence in depth) and changed column names, and drop every other field.
Pass `lock_timeout=0` to run_project from `preview` too, so a busy stage returns the same 'stage is busy, try again later' reply as `run`.
Reuse the run tool's exception mapping. Invalid YAML and validation problems come back as their already-sanitized problem lines.

Add in-memory MCP tests: validate passing and failing (including invalid YAML); preview in dev and in a branch; preview refused for stage, prod and custom names before any build_* seam runs; preview with an unreachable target. Every response goes through `assert_no_secret`. Also add a test that the server lists exactly the tools built so far.
inputs: src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py (guard helper and serializer from the run tool)
phases.expectedResult: The `preview` and `validate` MCP tools, covered by in-memory tests that include refusals and secret-leak assertions.
guardNotes: g3: every new branch in both tools is covered by unit tests; no pragma.
g6: no mcp import outside interface.

rubric.label: validate checks the Project without any Environment or connection
rubric.ruleStatement: The `validate(pipeline)` tool has no environment or branch parameter. It delegates to validate_project, returns problems, skipped Pipelines and Schedules as plain lists, and turns invalid YAML into its sanitized problem lines. 10 = tests cover pass, fail and invalid YAML, every build_* seam and lock spy records zero calls, and every response passes assert_no_secret. 8 = these are covered except the zero-seam assertion. Below 8 = validate takes or uses an Environment, or invalid YAML returns a traceback or 'unexpected' message.
passCriteria: Listing the tool's input schema through the in-memory session shows only an optional `pipeline` property.

Tests call validate on a valid Project (no problems), on a Project with a validation problem (the problem text is returned), and on a Project with broken adops.yaml (the sanitized YAML problem line is returned, not 'unexpected ...').
In those tests the run_command.build_* spies and the FakeLocks fixture record no calls.
`grep -n 'validate_project' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows delegation, with no re-implemented checks.
failureExamples: validate goes through the Environment guard and asks for 'dev', so it fails on Projects whose dev shares a target, even though validation never connects. This is a plausible over-reuse of the guard.
An invalid YAML file raises inside load_project_settings, is not in the mapping, and comes back as 'unexpected YAMLError'.

rubric.label: preview returns counts, at most 5 sample keys and column names, never row values
rubric.ruleStatement: For each Reverse Sync step, `preview` returns only the Preview counts, at most 5 sample keys per change kind, and the names of changed columns, plus any failing step's redacted error. Row values never appear. It refuses if any Preview reports written. 10 = a test feeds a Preview with more than 5 keys per kind and distinctive row values, then asserts the 5-key cap and that the values are absent. 8 = the cap and the field allowlist are tested, but row-value absence is only shown by inspection. Below 8 = sample rows or values are passed through.
passCriteria: A test makes the fake reverse-sync seam return a Preview with 8 inserted, 8 updated and 8 deleted sample keys. The response has at most 5 keys per kind and the full counts.
The same test plants a row value such as 'ROWVALUE-zz9' in any sample-row field the port carries, and the serialized response does not contain it.
A test with written=True returns a refusal error.
The response has no keys for non-Reverse-Sync step data (rows loaded, checks), so preview's output differs from run's.
failureExamples: The tool reuses run's serializer as is and returns the whole run payload, not just the Preview. This is plausible because the plan says to reuse the serializer.
The tool trusts that the port already caps samples and does not apply the 5-key limit itself, so a port change would leak more.

rubric.label: preview shares run's guard, refusals and fail-fast lock
rubric.ruleStatement: Derived from the acceptance criteria 'The MCP server's tools act only for dev and Branch Environments' and 'Stage and prod requests are refused in the server's own code': `preview` calls the same guard helper as `run` before run_project, refuses stage, prod and custom names before any seam runs, and passes lock_timeout=0 so a busy stage returns the same busy reply as run. 10 = all of these are tested, including the busy reply for a branch preview and an unreachable target. 8 = refusals and busy are tested, and the unreachable target is not. Below 8 = preview has its own copy of the Environment check, or blocks on a held lock.
passCriteria: Tests call preview with 'stage', 'prod' and a custom name. Each is an error, and the build_* spies and FakeLocks record zero calls.
Tests run preview in dev and in a branch, both succeeding with the Preview payload.
A test holding the lock through FakeLocks gets the same busy reply text as the run tool's busy test.
A test with an unreachable target returns the error_lines output for that error.
`grep -c '_guard\|assistant_target' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` shows a single guard definition used by both tools, not a second inline check.
failureExamples: preview calls run_project directly and copies the `environment == 'dev'` check but forgets refuse_shared_dev_connection. This is a plausible copy-paste drift.
lock_timeout=0 is passed in run but missed in preview, so a busy stage hangs the Assistant.

rubric.label: Every response from the new tools is scanned for secrets, and the tool set is exact
rubric.ruleStatement: Verbatim acceptance criterion: 'Tests assert that no MCP response contains a secret value.' Every new validate and preview test result goes through assert_no_secret, and a test asserts that list_tools returns exactly {run, preview, validate}, so no unguarded tool can sneak in. 10 = both hold, and a validate failure whose problem text would naturally mention a connection is scanned too. 8 = both hold. Below 8 = any new tool response is unscanned, or the tool list is checked as a subset.
passCriteria: `grep -c 'assert_no_secret' tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py` increases by at least the number of new call_tool uses.
A test calls session.list_tools() and asserts that the set of names == {'run', 'preview', 'validate'}.

Guard outcome: `uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-report=term-missing` reports 100% for src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py with no pragma (the repo keeps 100% line and branch coverage on the adops package).
failureExamples: The tool-list test uses `issubset`, so a leftover debug tool passes. This is a plausible lenient assertion.
The validate tests skip assert_no_secret because 'validate never connects'. Its problem lines can still echo .env-derived values.

rubric.label: The new tools stay thin interface adapters
rubric.ruleStatement: validate and preview are synchronous functions in mcp_server.py that delegate to validate_project and run_project and reuse the existing exception mapping. No logic moves into domain or application, and no new module imports mcp. 10 = only the two listed files change, and each tool body is guard, delegate and map. 8 = a small private helper is added in the same file. Below 8 = Preview filtering or Environment logic is added to application or domain for MCP's sake, or a tool is async.
passCriteria: `git diff --stat` for this phase lists only src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py and tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py.
`grep -rnE '^(from|import) mcp' src/adops` still lists only src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py.
`grep -nE 'async def (validate|preview)' src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py` returns nothing.
failureExamples: A `summarize_preview_for_assistant` function is added to adops/application, which leaks an interface presentation concern inward. This is a plausible 'clean architecture' move in the wrong direction.
preview is written as `async def` to call an async helper, which lets two runs overlap while os.environ is swapped.

phases.healerHint: If preview leaks run data or skips a refusal, give it its own small serializer that keeps only the counts, the first 5 sample keys per kind and the changed column names, and make sure its first statement calls the same guard helper `run` uses, with lock_timeout=0.

successCriteria: This horizon is done when ALL hold: (1) `adops mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio, and `adops init` / `adops init --demo` write a .mcp.json registering it (pinned by init tests and the ci.yml wheel list). (2) The server lists exactly the tools run, preview and validate. run and preview accept only the Environment named exactly `dev` or a branch name; unit tests show stage, prod, qa, production, Dev, 'dev ' and a custom name each get a sanitized refusal before any Warehouse, Source, target or file is touched. (3) run and preview on dev are refused when dev's Warehouse or any dev Reverse Sync target is the same database connection as stage's or prod's (normalized Postgres host/port/database, resolved DuckDB path), with a test per case; the demo Project's dev uses its own shop_dev target so the demo is not refused. (4) A Branch run through MCP works when stage's Warehouse Secret Reference is set, fails with a sanitized error naming it when not, only ever Previews, and returns 'stage is busy' at once when stage's Warehouse lock is held (the CLI keeps its 30-minute wait). (5) An in-memory MCP secret-leak suite sets a distinctive value for every Secret Reference and asserts no response of run, preview or validate, on success and failure paths (invalid YAML, missing Secret Reference, unreachable Warehouse, unexpected error), contains any secret value. (6) Engine output never reaches the stdio protocol stream. (7) CI stays green: uv sync --locked with mcp in pyproject.toml and uv.lock, ruff, 100% line+branch coverage, no new pragma, no mcp/typer imports in domain/application, Docker E2E within 20 minutes. The remaining vision item-7 tools (edit, read/list files, project view, test-connection, read-logs, drop-branch, accept-schema) and run logs are later horizons.

Add the adops mcp server with a run tool: A working `adops mcp` stdio server exposing a `run` tool that refuses every Environment except exact `dev` and Branch Environments, with in-memory MCP tests that assert no response contains a secret value.
Add a separate shop_dev target for demo dev: A demo template whose dev Reverse Sync target is the separate `shop_dev` database, created by a new seed script, with init and E2E tests passing.
Add .mcp.json to the init templates: Both init templates ship a .mcp.json registering `adops mcp`, pinned by the init tests and the ci.yml wheel list.
Add the preview and validate MCP tools: The `preview` and `validate` MCP tools, covered by in-memory tests that include refusals and secret-leak assertions.
